Error.NoGM: A GM needs to be connected for that.
Error.Timeout: The GM didn't answer in time.
Error.GMOnly: Only the GM can do that.

Notify.CltFound: Neon Combat Manager found Condition Lab & Triggler's conditions in this world. Open the Condition Lab to bring them over.

lightlyWounded.name: Lightly Wounded
lightlyWounded.hint: Below full HP. No penalty yet.

seriouslyWounded.name: Seriously Wounded
seriouslyWounded.hint: Under half HP: -2 to all Actions (Cyberpunk RED applies it).

mortallyWounded.name: Mortally Wounded
mortallyWounded.hint: Under 1 HP: -4 to all Actions, -6 MOVE and a Death Save at the start of each Turn (Cyberpunk RED applies the penalties). -6 MOVE (minimum 1).

dead.name: Dead
dead.hint: Failed a Death Save. Flatlined and marked defeated.

unconscious.name: Unconscious
unconscious.hint: Helpless: melee auto-hits. Wakes on damage or an Action to rouse them (unless choked or drugged).

stabilized.name: Stabilized
stabilized.hint: Patched up. A Mortally Wounded character goes to 1 HP and is out for a minute; the Death Save penalty resets to its base.

dismemberedArm.name: Dismembered Arm
dismemberedArm.hint: The arm is gone and whatever it held drops. Death Save penalty +1.

dismemberedHand.name: Dismembered Hand
dismemberedHand.hint: The hand is gone and whatever it held drops. Death Save penalty +1.

brokenRibs.name: Broken Ribs
brokenRibs.hint: Moving more than 4 m/yds on foot in a Turn reopens it: 5 damage straight to HP at the end of that Turn.

brokenArm.name: Broken Arm
brokenArm.hint: The arm can't be used and whatever it held drops.

foreignObject.name: Foreign Object
foreignObject.hint: Moving more than 4 m/yds on foot in a Turn: 5 damage straight to HP at the end of that Turn.

brokenLeg.name: Broken Leg
brokenLeg.hint: -4 MOVE (minimum 1) and -2 to Evasion. Each broken leg is its own injury: both broken is -4 Evasion.

spinalInjury.name: Spinal Injury
spinalInjury.hint: No Action next Turn (the Move Action is still there). Death Save penalty +1.

crushedFingers.name: Crushed Fingers
crushedFingers.hint: -4 to Actions that use that hand.

dismemberedLeg.name: Dismembered Leg
dismemberedLeg.hint: -6 MOVE (minimum 1) and no dodging. Death Save penalty +1. Martial Arts Recovery can't stand you up for free.

lostEye.name: Lost Eye
lostEye.hint: -4 to ranged attacks and Perception by sight. Death Save penalty +1.

brainInjury.name: Brain Injury
brainInjury.hint: -2 to all Actions. Death Save penalty +1.

damagedEye.name: Damaged Eye
damagedEye.hint: -2 to ranged attacks and Perception by sight.

foreignObjectHead.name: Foreign Object (Head)
foreignObjectHead.hint: Moving more than 4 m/yds on foot in a Turn: 5 damage straight to HP at the end of that Turn.

crackedSkull.name: Cracked Skull
crackedSkull.hint: Aimed Shots to the head multiply damage through SP by 3 instead of 2. Death Save penalty +1.

damagedEar.name: Damaged Ear
damagedEar.hint: -2 to Perception by hearing. After moving more than 4 m/yds in a Turn, no Move Action next Turn.

lostEar.name: Lost Ear
lostEar.hint: -4 to Perception by hearing. After moving more than 4 m/yds in a Turn, no Move Action next Turn. Death Save penalty +1.

prone.name: Prone
prone.hint: On the ground: no Move Action until an Action is spent to Get Up. -4 Evasion against melee and to resist or break a Grapple (toggles in the roll dialog). Within 2 m/yds of cover, attacks from that side are at -4 (-6 Heavy Weapons).

grappled.name: Grappled
grappled.hint: Held: -2 to all Actions, no Move Action (dragged along) and no two-handed weapons.

grappling.name: Grappling
grappling.hint: Holding someone: -2 to all Actions and no two-handed weapons. Let go any time.

ironGrip.name: Iron Grip
ironGrip.hint: Locked in: escape attempts take a further -2 (in the roll dialog) and no ranged attacks until the Grapple breaks.

choking1.name: Choked (1 Round)
choking1.hint: Choked this Round. Three Rounds in a row and they're Unconscious.

choking2.name: Choked (2 Rounds)
choking2.hint: Choked two Rounds running. One more and they're Unconscious.

humanShield.name: Human Shield
humanShield.hint: Being held up as cover: can't dodge ranged attacks and takes the hits meant for the holder.

cover.name: In Cover
cover.hint: Fully behind something that stops bullets, out of the attacker's line of sight.

hidden.name: Hidden
hidden.hint: Out of sight: enemies attack you and dodge your attacks at -4. Attacking gives you away.

readiedAction.name: Holding Action
readiedAction.hint: Holding an Action for a named trigger or a set Initiative number.

suppressed.name: Suppressed
suppressed.hint: Lost against Suppressive Fire: the next Move Action (and Run, if needed) goes to reaching cover.

netrunning.name: Netrunning
netrunning.hint: Jacked into the NET; their meat body is busy and exposed.

blind.name: Blinded
blind.hint: Can't see: everything that needs sight counts as obscured (-4).

flashbanged.name: Flashbanged
flashbanged.hint: A Damaged Eye and a Damaged Ear for a minute (no Bonus Damage). Anti-Dazzle stops it.

teargassed.name: Teargassed
teargassed.hint: Damaged Eye effects for a minute, with no bonus damage. Only meat eyes are affected.

sleep.name: Knocked Out (Sleep)
sleep.hint: Prone and Unconscious for a minute, or until hurt or shaken awake.

emp.name: EMP'd
emp.hint: Two pieces of cyberware or carried electronics, the GM's pick, are dead for a minute.

onFireMild.name: On Fire (Mild)
onFireMild.hint: 2 damage straight to HP at the end of each Turn, until an Action is spent putting it out.

onFireStrong.name: On Fire (Strong)
onFireStrong.hint: 4 damage straight to HP at the end of each Turn, until an Action is spent putting it out.

onFireDeadly.name: On Fire (Deadly)
onFireDeadly.hint: 6 damage straight to HP at the end of each Turn, until an Action is spent putting it out.

drowning.name: Drowning
drowning.hint: BODY in damage straight to HP at the start of each Turn.

asphyxiating.name: Asphyxiating
asphyxiating.hint: Treated like drowning: BODY in damage straight to HP at the start of each Turn.

electrocuted.name: Electrocuted
electrocuted.hint: 6d6 (armor applies) at the end of each Turn while still touching the source.

radiationLow.name: Radiation (Low)
radiationLow.hint: Slow harm over time; the long-term cost is the GM's call.

radiationHigh.name: Radiation (High)
radiationHigh.hint: In a hot zone: burns like a Mild fire (2 a Turn) that can't be put out while there.

falling.name: Falling
falling.hint: Drops 40 m/yds at the end of the Turn; 2d6 per 10 m/yds on landing and a DV15 Athletics Check or a Broken Leg.

exposure.name: Exposure
exposure.hint: Out in extreme weather without the right gear: 1d6 straight to HP each day and no natural healing.

smoke.name: In Smoke
smoke.hint: Obscured by smoke for a minute: -4 to anything that needs sight.

antibiotics.name: Antibiotics
antibiotics.hint: Heals 2 extra HP a day for a week once natural healing has begun.

rapidetox.name: Rapidetox
rapidetox.hint: Purges drugs, poisons and intoxicants at once. Addictions stay.

speedheal.name: Speedheal
speedheal.hint: Heals BODY + WILL HP at once, unless Mortally Wounded. Once a day.

stim.name: Stim
stim.hint: Ignores the Seriously Wounded penalty for an hour. Once a day.

surge.name: Surge
surge.hint: No need for sleep for 24 hours. Once a week.

blackLace.name: Black Lace
blackLace.hint: 24 hours ignoring the Seriously Wounded penalty. Costs 2d6 Humanity, given back if they don't get hooked.

blackLaceAddiction.name: Black Lace Addiction
blackLaceAddiction.hint: -2 REF, except while on Black Lace.

blueGlass.name: Blue Glass
blueGlass.hint: 4 hours of sudden hallucinations: a flash out costs that Turn's Action.

blueGlassAddiction.name: Blue Glass Addiction
blueGlassAddiction.hint: Flashes out now and then, except while on Blue Glass.

boost.name: Boost
boost.hint: 24 hours of +2 INT (it can go above 8).

smash.name: Smash
smash.hint: 4 hours of +2 to Dance, Contortionist, Conversation, Human Perception, Persuasion and Acting.

smashAddiction.name: Smash Addiction
smashAddiction.hint: -2 to Dance, Contortionist, Conversation, Human Perception, Persuasion and Acting; cravings.

synthcoke.name: Synthcoke
synthcoke.hint: 4 hours of +1 REF (it can go above 8), and paranoia.

synthcokeAddiction.name: Synthcoke Addiction
synthcokeAddiction.hint: -2 REF, except while on Synthcoke; cravings.

wxLightRain.name: Light Rain
wxLightRain.hint: Slick underfoot: -1 to climbing, driving and the like when the GM calls for it (in the roll dialog).

wxHeavyRain.name: Heavy Rain
wxHeavyRain.hint: Hard to see: -2 to sight and ranged attacks at a distance. Slick: -1 to footing and driving when called for.

wxAcidRain.name: Acid Rain
wxAcidRain.hint: Each full minute out in it without an umbrella or waterproof lining ablates worn armor by 1.

wxBloodRain.name: Blood Rain
wxBloodRain.hint: -1 to sight. Each minute it acts like acid rain or a dose of Biotoxin; an umbrella or lining gives +2 to resist.

wxAshStorm.name: Ash Storm
wxAshStorm.hint: -2 to sight. A minute in it without a mask or Nasal Filters: a dose of poison and a Foreign Object.

wxDustStorm.name: Dust Storm
wxDustStorm.hint: -2 to sight. Five minutes in it without a mask or Nasal Filters: a Foreign Object.

wxInversionSmog.name: Inversion Smog
wxInversionSmog.hint: -4 to sight. A minute in it without a mask or Nasal Filters: a dose of poison.

wxThunderstorm.name: Deadly Thunderstorm
wxThunderstorm.hint: -2 to sight. Every ten minutes lightning may hit the tallest thing around, or whoever holds a two-handed metal weapon.

wxRadioactiveWind.name: Radioactive Windstorm
wxRadioactiveWind.hint: High radiation for anyone without a Radiation Suit.

wxColdSnap.name: Cold Snap
wxColdSnap.hint: Below freezing: Exposure without cold-weather gear. Black ice: -2 to footing and driving when called for.

wxHeatWave.name: Heat Wave
wxHeatWave.hint: Exposure without hot-weather gear. Armor penalties to REF, DEX and MOVE are 2 worse (1 with a hot-weather lining).

wxHot.name: Hot
wxHot.hint: Armor penalties to REF, DEX and MOVE are 1 worse (none with a hot-weather lining).

wxCold.name: Cold
wxCold.hint: Exposure for anyone out most of the day without cold-weather gear.

wxFlooding.name: Flooding
wxFlooding.hint: Wading through deep water costs 2 m/yds of movement per m/yd.

wxBlackout.name: Blackout
wxBlackout.hint: No power, no CitiNet and no Agent calls in the area.

lowLight.name: Low Light
lowLight.hint: Night or poor lighting: -1 to anything that needs sight.

darkness.name: Darkness
darkness.hint: Too dark to see: -4 to anything that needs sight.

obscured.name: Obscured
obscured.hint: Rain, smog, dust or smoke in the way: a penalty to anything that needs sight.

intoTheWall.name: Into the Wall
intoTheWall.hint: Thrown, Lariated or blown back into cover: Spinal Injury for one Round (no Bonus Damage).

stakesBonus.name: Plot Die Bonus
stakesBonus.hint: The Plot Die's +2/+4 on this Check. Gone once the Check is rolled.

stakesAided.name: Aided (+2)
stakesAided.hint: An ally's Opportunity: +2 to the next Check. Gone once it's rolled.

stakesHindered.name: Hindered
stakesHindered.hint: A Complication: a penalty on the next Check. Gone once it's rolled.

qhCommsJam.name: Comms Jam
qhCommsJam.hint: No calls, texts or messages in or out for 20 Rounds (the Holocall buttons won't call out).

qhVitalsSpoof.name: Vitals Spoof
qhVitalsSpoof.hint: For an hour their Biomonitor shows calm, normal vitals: no alarm, no Trauma Team call.

qhPopupGeddon.name: PopUp-geddon
qhPopupGeddon.hint: Ads all over the HUD: -2 to Checks that need sight for 3 Rounds.

qhImpairMovement.name: Impair Movement
qhImpairMovement.hint: MOVE -1 for 20 Rounds. At MOVE 0, no Move Actions.

qhShortCircuit.name: Short Circuit
qhShortCircuit.hint: Three pieces of chrome (the GM picks; not limbs, eyes, audio, Neuroport or Cybersuite) are off for 20 Rounds.

qhCyberwareMalfunction.name: Cyberware Malfunction
qhCyberwareMalfunction.hint: One piece of chrome and its options are off for 20 Rounds. A limb acts as Broken.

qhRebootOptics.name: Reboot Optics
qhRebootOptics.hint: Cybereyes down for 3 Rounds: all-chrome eyes are blind (-4 to sight, no dodging ranged attacks). Action + DV13 Cybertech restarts them.

qhCrippleMovement.name: Cripple Movement
qhCrippleMovement.hint: Cyberlegs lock: no Move Actions for 2 Rounds, then MOVE -2 until 20 Rounds are up.

qhWeaponGlitch.name: Weapon Glitch
qhWeaponGlitch.hint: The smart-linked weapon jams (an Action to clear) and is -2 to hit for 3 Rounds.

qhLimbSeize.name: Limb Seize
qhLimbSeize.hint: One cyberarm goes limp for 3 Rounds: drops what it holds, popups retract, options off.

qhSpeedwareCrash.name: Speedware Crash
qhSpeedwareCrash.hint: Speedware off for 20 Rounds. If it was running: its bonus is gone and 1d6 to HP.

qhSonicShock.name: Sonic Shock
qhSonicShock.hint: Damaged Ear (no Bonus Damage) for 20 Rounds.

qhFrameLock.name: Frame Lock
qhFrameLock.hint: The frame seizes for 3 Rounds: no Move Actions and -4 to physical Actions (untick it for others).

qhQKrash.name: Q-KRASH
qhQKrash.hint: Their deck can't run quickhacks for 20 Rounds, or until cleared with an Action and DV13 Electronics/Security Tech.

qhSystemReset.name: System Reset
qhSystemReset.hint: Unconscious and Prone for 20 Rounds, or until damaged.

qhPuppet.name: Puppet
qhPuppet.hint: The Netrunner controls their Action and Move Action next Turn.

qhCyberpsychosis.name: Cyberpsychosis (hack)
qhCyberpsychosis.hint: For 3 Rounds they attack the nearest person. Then 2d6 Humanity Loss.

chromeSandevistan.name: Sandevistan
chromeSandevistan.hint: Speedware running: +3 Initiative for a minute (their place in a fight already under way moves up 3, and drops back when it stops). An Action to start; 1-hour cooldown.

chromeApogee.name: Sandevistan: Apogee OS
chromeApogee.hint: Militech 'Apogee' running for 3 Rounds: +6 Initiative, +2 to Aimed Shots, dodges bullets whatever their REF, no MOVE or Evasion penalties. Free to start, even out of turn. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: 1d6 Humanity Loss each time. 20-Round cooldown.

chromeProfessional.name: Sandevistan: Professional OS
chromeProfessional.hint: Dynalar 'Professional' running for 3 Rounds: +3 Initiative, and their Move Action comes as if first in Initiative. Starts as half of a ROF2 Action.

chromeWarpDancer.name: Sandevistan: Warp Dancer OS
chromeWarpDancer.hint: Qiant 'Warp Dancer' running for 4 Rounds: +3 Initiative, and small jobs (get up, Reload, clear a jam...) take half of a ROF2 Action, each once a Turn. 1-hour cooldown.

chromeFalcon.name: Sandevistan: Falcon OS
chromeFalcon.hint: Militech 'Falcon' running for 3 Rounds: +4 Initiative, dodges bullets whatever their REF; each Turn, +2 MOVE or +4 on one Evasion Check. Free to start. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: 1d6 Humanity Loss each time. 1-hour cooldown.

chromeReflexPlus.name: Sandevistan: Reflex-Plus OS
chromeReflexPlus.hint: Zetatech 'Reflex-Plus' running for 5 Rounds: +3 Initiative and +1 REF (not with Synthcoke). Starts as half of a ROF2 Action. 1-hour cooldown.

chromeBerserk.name: Berserk
chromeBerserk.hint: Berserk running for a minute: no Seriously or Mortally Wounded penalties (the automatic Critical Injuries and Death Saves stay). An Action to start; 1-hour cooldown.

chromeKerenzikov.name: Kerenzikov
chromeKerenzikov.hint: A Kerenzikov, always on from the day it's installed: you can dodge ranged attacks whatever your REF, and get +2 to notice an Ambush (a tick box on Perception rolls). With a Kerenzikov Boost System fitted it's Speedware, with +2 Initiative always. Its player's screen runs a shade cooler, as if the world were a touch slow.

chromeOpticalCamo.name: Optical Camo
chromeOpticalCamo.hint: Optical Camo running for a minute, until you attack, Run or get hit: free Stealth Checks even in plain sight, Perception against you at −4, and nobody targets you without beating your Stealth with Perception. An Action to start; 10-minute recharge. The token stays where everyone can see it: who can see the character is the table's call.

chromeMicrorotors.name: Microrotors
chromeMicrorotors.hint: Microrotors running for 2 Rounds: two-handed and cyberlimb melee weapons go from ROF1 to ROF2, and ROF2 ones can make Aimed Shots at ROF2. An Action to start; 10-Round cooldown.

chromeKers.name: KERS Mask
chromeKers.hint: The reflection system is on: your face is masked, cameras included. −2 to Human Perception and Lip Reading against you. An Action to switch on or off.

tactileBoost.name: Feeling for Motion
tactileBoost.hint: Tactile Boost, with a hand flat on a surface: you feel anything moving within 20 m/yds, walls or not, as a ripple where it last moved. That hand does nothing else while you do. Needs Sequencer for the ripples.

chromeBerserker.name: Berserk: Berserker OS
chromeBerserker.hint: Biodyne 'Berserker' running for 5 Rounds: Berserk, with small jobs as half of a ROF2 Action; once a Round a melee hit for 4+ counts as two for Martial Arts. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: -4 to ranged attacks.

chromeBaldur.name: Berserk: Baldur OS
chromeBaldur.hint: Militech 'Baldur' running for 4 Rounds: Berserk, all HP damage halved (round up), Brawling and Martial Arts Aimed Shots at ROF2; 5 HP back when it stops. Free to start. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: 1d6 Humanity Loss each time and -4 to ranged attacks. 1-hour cooldown.

chromeMatterhorn.name: Berserk: Matterhorn OS
chromeMatterhorn.hint: Moore Tech 'Matterhorn' running for 10 Rounds: Berserk, the first damage each Round cut by half their BODY, Critical Injury penalties halved. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: -4 to ranged attacks.

chromeBrawler.name: Berserk: Brawler OS
chromeBrawler.hint: Zetatech 'Brawler' running for 5 Rounds: Berserk, all damage 2 less before armor, limbs hit like cyberlimbs, no automatic Critical Injuries while Mortally Wounded. Without an FBC or Cyberspine: -4 to ranged attacks. 1-hour cooldown.

awareSuspicious.name: Suspicious
awareSuspicious.hint: Heard something: head up, looking around, not searching yet. Stealth DV 11 + the number of enemies. Back to Unaware after a minute of nothing (GM option).

awareSearching.name: Searching
awareSearching.hint: Looking for someone. The Stealth DV is the closest enemy's Perception roll. Back to Suspicious after 10 minutes of nothing (GM option).

awareAlert.name: Alert
awareAlert.hint: They know someone's here: weapons up, doors locked. The Stealth DV is the highest Perception roll among them, and the security response is on its way. Kept until something is done about it.

awareSpotted.name: Spotted
awareSpotted.hint: They see you. No more sneaking: roll Initiative.

tarotWinded.name: Winded (Justice)
tarotWinded.hint: The wind knocked out of them: -5 Evasion against melee and no dodging ranged attacks, for a minute.

tarotNoPain.name: No Pain (The Tower)
tarotNoPain.hint: For an hour they feel no pain and ignore the Seriously Wounded penalty.

tarotChromeShutdown.name: Chrome Shutdown (The Fool)
tarotChromeShutdown.hint: All their cyberware is off for an hour, Neuroport included. Cyberlimbs hang limp like dismembered limbs. With no other way to sense the enemy, another -4 to every Check.

tarotFated.name: Fated (The Empress)
tarotFated.hint: The next three successful attacks against them this combat each cause a Critical Injury, whatever the dice say.

extremeCyberpsychosis.name: Extreme Cyberpsychosis
extremeCyberpsychosis.hint: Humanity below 0: a complete psychotic break. The GM plays the character until Humanity is positive again (Immunoblockers can bring them back). Each Round, 1 LUCK buys a try at retaking the Move Action or the Action. The +2 is the GM's call.

powerRebuild.name: Power Weapon
powerRebuild.hint: A Power gun in hand: +5 Bonus Damage on its Critical Injuries, and ricochets at -4 off cover to hit a target you know is there but can't see (Aimed: only the -8).

smartRebuild.name: Smart Weapon
smartRebuild.hint: A Smart gun in hand: +1 to its attacks with a Personal Link or Subdermal Grip, on the roll as Smart weapon. Improved Smart Ammunition ignores visual obscurement, and a miss by 5 or less gets a second try at 14 + 1d10 (+ LUCK), the first shot's penalties still applying.

weaponStrain.name: Weapon Strain
weaponStrain.hint: Holding a weapon without the BODY (or the paired cyberarms) its card asks for: the penalties to REF, DEX or MOVE the card gives, for as long as it's in hand. Stow it and they go; whether it's mounted is the GM's call.

improvedSmart.name: Improved Smart Loaded
improvedSmart.hint: Improved Smart Ammunition in a Smart gun in hand. Its attacks ignore every visual obscurement penalty (Low Light, Darkness, Obscured, smoke, pop-ups, weather's sight penalties): they come off the roll before its dialog opens, and the card says how much. A miss by 5 or less gets a second try at 14 + 1d10 (+ LUCK). The gun's own +1 shows on the roll as Smart weapon.

monoRebuild.name: Mono-edge Weapon
monoRebuild.hint: A blade with Mono-edge Blading or the Monoblade Rebuild in hand: its damage ignores armor below its SP (7, 11 or 13 by tier).

techRebuild.name: Tech Weapon
techRebuild.hint: A Tech gun in hand: its scope shows outlines through thin cover. Charge it with the Move Action (20 Rounds or until fired): the next shot is ROF 1, goes through thin cover without damaging it and ignores half the target's SP.

carouselEnabled.name: Show the combat carousel
carouselEnabled.hint: The Initiative Queue as cards across the top of the screen while a combat is on.

carouselSize.name: Carousel size
carouselSize.hint: How big the combatant cards are.

carouselPlacement.name: Carousel position
carouselPlacement.hint: At the very top of the play area (over the scene tabs), or just under the scene tabs.

encounterMode.name: Begin a combat as
encounterMode.hint: What a combat begun from Foundry's combat tracker or a macro is: a fight, or a stealth segment (Turns and Rounds in Initiative order, the enemies' Awareness left where it is). On the carousel the GM picks Sneak or Start, and can switch at any time.

roundSeconds.name: Seconds per Round
roundSeconds.hint: World time each new Round adds. Cyberpunk RED: about 3 seconds (a minute is 20 Rounds). SmallTime and Neon Hub's calendar follow world time.

turnSeconds.name: Seconds per Turn
turnSeconds.hint: Extra world time for each Turn skipped when a Round is cut short. 0 keeps a Round at its full length.

combatSummary.name: Post how long a combat took
combatSummary.hint: When a combat ends, post its Rounds, the time that passed and the time of day.

npcHealth.name: What players see of NPC health
npcHealth.hint: In the carousel and tracker: nothing, the Wound State, or the HP bar.

enhanceTracker.name: Add Wound States to the combat tracker
enhanceTracker.hint: Shows each combatant's Wound State and the combat clock in Foundry's sidebar tracker.

deathSaves.name: Death Save prompts
deathSaves.hint: At the start of a Mortally Wounded character's Turn, post a card to roll the Death Save (a failure flatlines them).

hazardDamage.name: Damage from conditions
hazardDamage.hint: Fire, drowning, radiation and reopened Critical Injuries: post a card the GM applies, apply it at once, or do nothing.

pickupCarried.name: Picked-up items are Carried
pickupCarried.hint: An item taken out of an Item Piles pile goes onto the character as Carried, ready for Equip / Change Weapon in the Action HUD. Without Item Piles, the same goes for an item dropped on a character's token or sheet.

trackMovement.name: Track movement for Critical Injuries
trackMovement.hint: Add up how far the acting token moves each Turn, for Broken Ribs, Foreign Objects and damaged ears (over 4 m/yds).

replaceStatuses.name: Replace Foundry's token statuses
replaceStatuses.hint: Use the Cyberpunk RED set in the token HUD instead of Foundry's generic one. Other modules' statuses stay.

conditionChat.name: Condition notices in chat
conditionChat.hint: Post a card when a condition is added: off, to its owners and the GM, or to everyone.

mirrorWounds.name: Show Wound States on tokens
mirrorWounds.hint: Lightly, Seriously and Mortally Wounded appear as statuses (Cyberpunk RED already applies their penalties).

mirrorCriticals.name: Show Critical Injuries on tokens
mirrorCriticals.hint: A Critical Injury item on an actor shows as a status on its token.

critItems.name: Critical Injury conditions add Cyberpunk RED's item
critItems.hint: Placing a Critical Injury condition gives the actor the system's own Critical Injury item, whose effect carries the penalties.

cltShim.name: Stand in for Condition Lab & Triggler
cltShim.hint: When Condition Lab & Triggler isn't running, provide game.clt (addCondition, removeCondition, hasCondition...) so macros and modules written for it keep working.

weatherSource.name: Weather comes from
weatherSource.hint: Neon Hub's calendar weather, the GM's manual pick in the Environment window, or nowhere.

sceneWeatherDefault.name: Scenes are
sceneWeatherDefault.hint: Whether weather reaches scenes that don't say. Set each scene in its configuration (Ambience tab); roof tiles that restrict weather or are ticked "Shelters from weather", Suppress Weather regions and regions named like a shelter keyword keep characters out of it.

shelterKeywords.name: Shelter region keywords
shelterKeywords.hint: Tokens inside a scene region whose name contains one of these (comma-separated) are out of the weather.

weatherOnByDefault.name: Weather sight penalties start ticked
weatherOnByDefault.hint: Weather's penalty to sight and ranged attacks is ticked in the roll dialog. Off: the player or GM ticks it when it applies.

weatherHazardCards.name: Weather hazard cards
weatherHazardCards.hint: During combat, tell the GM when acid rain, smog, ash, dust or lightning comes due, with buttons to apply it.

visibilityEnabled.name: Visibility from light
visibilityEnabled.hint: Darkness and light sources set a Low Light (-1) or Darkness (-4) condition on the characters in the encounter.

lowLightAt.name: Low light from darkness
lowLightAt.hint: Scene darkness (0-1) from which it counts as low light. SmallTime moves the darkness with the clock.

darkAt.name: Dark from darkness
darkAt.hint: Scene darkness (0-1) from which an unlit spot counts as dark.

sightKeys.name: Checks that need sight
sightKeys.hint: Cyberpunk RED roll keys a sight penalty applies to (comma-separated), shown as situational modifiers in the roll dialog.

visibilityCap.name: Most a sight penalty can be
visibilityCap.hint: Darkness and weather add up to at most this (both count as being obscured). 0: no limit.

visibilityFrom.name: Light that counts
visibilityFrom.hint: The light where the target is (while a target is picked), or where the character stands.

envOutsideCombat.name: Environment outside combat
envOutsideCombat.hint: Also apply weather and visibility to every player token on the scene when there's no combat.

gearBreathing.name: Breathing protection
gearBreathing.hint: Items or cyberware (comma-separated names) that protect against smog, ash and dust.

gearRadiation.name: Radiation protection
gearRadiation.hint: Items that protect against radioactive wind.

gearRain.name: Rain protection
gearRain.hint: Items that protect against acid and blood rain.

gearCold.name: Cold-weather gear
gearCold.hint: Items that protect against Exposure from cold.

gearHeat.name: Hot-weather gear
gearHeat.hint: Items that protect against Exposure from heat and soften the heat's armor penalty.

gearVision.name: Sight enhancement
gearVision.hint: Cyberware that cancels darkness and obscurement penalties (Low Light/Infrared/UV).

combat.name: Combat & Time
combat.label: Combat & Time
combat.hint: Round length, NPC health, Death Saves and condition damage.

conditions.name: Neon Conditions
conditions.label: Conditions
conditions.hint: Token statuses, chat notices, Wound States, Critical Injuries and the Condition Lab & Triggler stand-in.

environment.name: Weather & Visibility
environment.label: Weather & Visibility
environment.hint: Night City weather from Neon Hub, light and darkness, shelter and protective gear.

comms.name: Biomon Link
comms.label: Biomon Link
comms.hint: What linking needs. Holocalls are Night City Messenger's: numbers, voicemail and call logs are set up in its Phone settings.

hub.name: City & NCART hub
hub.label: Map settings
hub.hint: Who can open the 2070 city map, and how map positions affect holocall signal.

rules.name: 2070 roller & table rules
rules.label: Roller & rules
rules.hint: The Plot Die in the roll dialog, Riding the Edge, Chain Reactions, Tarot Criticals, Flash of Luck and the Awareness Ladder.

chat.name: Neon Chat
chat.hint: Formatting, merged messages, editing, the Adventure Log and the visual novel stage.
chat.label: Chat & stage

fx.name: Neon FX
fx.label: Neon FX
fx.hint: Sequencer visuals for conditions, the Cyberpsychosis glitch and the Sandevistan, and their macros.

arsenal.name: Neon Arsenal
arsenal.label: Neon Arsenal
arsenal.hint: Automated Animations for 2070 weapons and ammo (JB2A), weapon sounds, area attacks that place their template, Diwako's DV display and muzzle flashes, and the weapon traits of Power, Smart and Tech guns and Rebuilds.

noSignalFx.name: "No signal" screen
noSignalFx.hint: A short glitch and fade when your view lands in a Night City Messenger dead zone (players only).

biomonAlerts.name: Biomon Link alarms
biomonAlerts.hint: When someone on your link goes critical, drops or flatlines: a notice, the Biomon window pops open, or nothing.

linkNeedsImplant.name: Biomon Link needs a Biomonitor or Neuroport
linkNeedsImplant.hint: Only characters with one of the implants below installed can link (it's the implant that broadcasts their vitals). A linked character whose implant comes out shows NO SIGNAL.

linkImplants.name: Implants that link
linkImplants.hint: Installed cyberware (comma-separated names) that broadcasts vitals: the CEMK Neuroport (and Neuroport (Free)) and Biomonitor cyberware by default.

holocallSheetButton.name: Holocall button on character sheets
holocallSheetButton.hint: Adds Holocall to the character sheet's header. Off by default, since sheet headers get crowded. Without it, use the Holocall macro (Neon Combat Manager: Macros compendium; drop it on the hotbar or the Action HUD), the Action HUD's Utility group, or Holocall in the Actors directory's right-click menu.

ncmSpam.name: Night City Messenger spam
ncmSpam.hint: Night City Messenger's built-in junk mail is set in 2045 (the red sky, the crater). 2070 swaps it for 2070s spam: a free city after the Unification War, Arasaka back in town, braindance, Trauma Team plans. The districts and corps its {{randomDistrict}} and {{randomCorpo}} draw from change too. Your own templates stay either way.

hubPlayers.name: Players can open the city map
hubPlayers.hint: Players see the places, districts, NCART and the crew. Off: only the GM.

hubSignal.name: Map position decides holocall signal
hubSignal.hint: A character pinned where the Utility Code is 9 or worse (West Wind, the Occupied Zone, Laguna Bend) has no signal and can't call out. Who can be reached is Night City Messenger's call, by its own networks and dead zones.

hubDeadZones.name: More dead zones
hubDeadZones.hint: District codes or names with no signal on top of those, separated by commas ("E, The Badlands").

hubSignalScenes.name: Dead ground mutes its scenes in Night City Messenger
hubSignalScenes.hint: A scene a place opens into (its doorway) becomes a Night City Messenger dead zone when the place stands on dead ground: no messages or calls while you're there. Dead zones you set in Night City Messenger yourself are left alone. Needs "Map position decides holocall signal".

hubDiscovery.name: Places are discovered
hubDiscovery.hint: Players only see the places you reveal (the 85 on the 2070 map and your own). Off: they see every place you haven't hidden.

hubRevealDossier.name: Reveal opens the dossier
hubRevealDossier.hint: When you reveal one place, its dossier opens full screen on the players' screens. Off: they get the chat card and the place on their map.

hubTravel.name: Players visit places from the map
hubTravel.hint: Places with a doorway the GM opened lead into their scenes. While a GM is online, the character's token lands on the doorway's tile and its Monk's Active Tiles actions run. Any time: players can go between sessions too (no GM: they view the scene and move their own token if allowed).

fireEscalates.name: Already On Fire
fireEscalates.hint: A fire that wouldn't raise someone's stage still pushes it up one: Mild to Strong, Strong to Deadly (2070 Core Rules).

wakeOnDamage.name: Damage wakes the unconscious
wakeOnDamage.hint: Unconscious (and System Reset) ends when the character takes damage, unless they're drugged asleep or being choked.

rollerHooks.name: 2070 roller
rollerHooks.hint: Hook into Cyberpunk RED's own rolls for the Plot Die bar, Riding the Edge, Chain Reactions and Tarot Criticals. Needs a reload.

rideEdge.name: Riding the Edge
rideEdge.hint: LUCK buys Push the Limit, Second Chance and Close Call instead of +1 a point (CPR's LUCK box is hidden).

chainReactions.name: Chain Reactions
chainReactions.hint: A second 10 on an explosion (or 1 on an implosion) chains: a card pays out Opportunities, Complications, damage or a Critical Injury.

tarotCriticals.name: Tarot Criticals
tarotCriticals.hint: Three or more 6s on a damage roll offer the GM a Major Arcana card instead of the normal Critical Injury (one a session).

flashOfLuck.name: Flash of Luck
flashOfLuck.hint: Players spend LUCK on flashbacks from the Plot Die window, with the GM's approval (one a Beat, three a Mission).

awarenessLadder.name: Awareness Ladder
awarenessLadder.hint: The GM sees the encounter's enemies' awareness (Unaware to Spotted) and the Stealth DV on the carousel.

combatRaisesAlert.name: Full combat puts the enemies at Alert
combatRaisesAlert.hint: When a fight begins, or a stealth segment turns into one, the Awareness Ladder goes up to Alert if it's lower (once: the GM can lower it again). A stealth segment never moves it.

awarenessTokens.name: Awareness on the tokens
awarenessTokens.hint: The encounter's enemies carry the Awareness Ladder's step as a condition, with a mark over each as it changes. Only Alert and Spotted (the rest stays the GM's, with a mark only the GM sees), every step for everyone, or not at all.

alertTimer.name: Alert: Rounds until the response is called
alertTimer.hint: When the enemies reach Alert, a countdown to the security response being called shows for everyone and runs on the game clock (20 Rounds is a minute). At zero the GM is told the response is called; the Alert stays. The GM can wave it away. 0: no countdown.

alertClears.name: An Alert clears when no one's left to raise it
alertClears.hint: With every enemy in the encounter dead or out before the response is called, the Alert ends and the Ladder goes back to Unaware. Once the response is called, the Alert stays until the GM moves the Ladder.

alertBanner.name: Alert on screen
alertBanner.hint: ALERT flashes across your screen when the enemies reach it, and the countdown to the security response shows while it runs. Its sounds follow your Neon FX volume.

hackFlow.name: Quickhacking on the Action HUD
hackFlow.hint: The Netrunning group gets Jack In, Ghost Jack In, Breach, the quickhacks slotted in the deck and Jack Out; someone being hacked gets Eject. Each rolls by the 2070 rules (Core Rules ch.10) and posts a card. Range, line of sight, NET Actions and a quickhack's Needs stay with the table.

actionHud.name: Action HUD
actionHud.hint: A bar of the controlled token's actions: Initiative, attacks, skills, role abilities and more, laid out your way (the sliders button customizes it).

chatPortraits.name: Chat portraits
chatPortraits.hint: The speaker's picture by their name in chat: the token's art or the actor's. Players talking out of character get their avatar.

rollPrivacyButtons.name: Roll privacy buttons
rollPrivacyButtons.hint: Four buttons (Public, GM, Blind, Self) instead of the roll mode dropdown under the chat box (Foundry v12).

chatCommandMenu.name: Chat command menu
chatCommandMenu.hint: Type / in the chat box for the commands you can use, with what each takes. @name starts a whisper.

chatSpeakAs.name: Speak-as menu
chatSpeakAs.hint: A menu over the chat box to choose who you speak as: yourself, or one of your characters in the scene you're viewing (or on stage).

stageShow.name: Show the stage
stageShow.hint: The visual novel stage on your screen. Off hides it for you only.

chatFormatting.name: Discord-style formatting
chatFormatting.hint: **bold**, *italic*, __underline__, ~~strike~~, ||spoilers||, `code`, > quotes, # headings, lists and [links](https://…) in chat messages.

chatMerge.name: Merge messages
chatMerge.hint: Messages from the same speaker a few minutes apart show as one block.

chatEditing.name: Edit sent messages
chatEditing.hint: Right-click your message (or press Up in an empty chat box) to edit it. The GM can edit anyone's.

adventureLog.name: Adventure Log
adventureLog.hint: /log keeps dated lines and quotes in a journal the players can read; /gmlog in the GM's own.

adventureLogName.name: Adventure Log journal
adventureLogName.hint: The journal's name (made the first time something is logged). Empty: "Adventure Log".

stageEnabled.name: The stage
stageEnabled.hint: Visual novel scenes: characters on stage as big portraits, their lines in dialogue boxes, expressions, and the narrator.

mirrorCyberpsychosis.name: Extreme Cyberpsychosis follows Humanity
mirrorCyberpsychosis.hint: Below 0 Humanity a character gets Extreme Cyberpsychosis; it goes once Humanity is positive again (2070 Core Rules, Chapter 09). One the GM placed by hand stays.

fxEnabled.name: Neon FX
fxEnabled.hint: Sequencer visuals for conditions, the Cyberpsychosis glitch and the Sandevistan. Needs the Sequencer module; uses JB2A when it's installed.

fxConditions.name: Condition visuals
fxConditions.hint: Tokens show their conditions: fire, electricity, glitching quickhacks, Mortally Wounded's heartbeat and more.

fxMacros.name: Neon FX macros
fxMacros.hint: Put the Sandevistan, Cyberpsychosis and Clear Neon FX macros in a "Neon FX" macro folder (once; delete or move them freely).

fxChrome.name: Speedware and Berserk conditions
fxChrome.hint: A Sandevistan, Berserk or one of their Operating Systems running is a condition on the character (Chrome running), whose token shows it: a burst as it kicks in, a look while it runs (each Operating System in its own colour), a ring as it stops. Switching the chrome's "(active)" effect, the Neon FX macros and the condition itself all stay in step, and Initiative in a fight moves with it.

fxScreen.name: Chrome on my screen
fxScreen.hint: While your own character's Sandevistan or Berserk runs, your screen shows it (the world drained and edged in the Operating System's colour; a red, beating rim for Berserk), and a Kerenzikov cools the picture slightly all the time. Only you see it; it never hides anything or takes a click. Off: no screen effect for you.

chromeTokenHud.name: Chrome switches on the Token HUD
chromeTokenHud.hint: A chip button on the Token HUD's right column lists the chrome the character can switch on and off (Sandevistan and Berserk with their Operating Systems, Tactile Boost, Optical Camo and the rest), lit while it runs.

fxTactile.name: Tactile Boost ripples
fxTactile.hint: A selected character Feeling for Motion (Tactile Boost, a hand on a surface) shows their player an amber ripple where anyone out of sight moves within 20 m/yds, through walls. Only that player sees it; GM-hidden tokens never show.

hackFx.name: Quickhack animations
hackFx.hint: Jack In, Breach, quickhacks, Self-ICE, detection and Jack Out play on the map: a link between the Netrunner and the target, the upload, and how it lands. Needs Sequencer; uses JB2A when it's installed.

hackGhostFx.name: Who sees a Ghost Hack
hackGhostFx.hint: A Ghosted Netrunner the target hasn't noticed: the dim link and uploads play for the GM and the Netrunner's players only, for everyone, or not at all. Once the Ghost is broken, everyone sees.

fxVolume.name: Neon FX volume
fxVolume.hint: How loud Neon FX's sounds are for you, on top of the channel's own slider. 0 silences them.

fxChannel.name: Neon FX sound channel
fxChannel.hint: Which of Foundry's volume sliders Neon FX's sounds follow.

fxMotion.name: Neon FX token motion
fxMotion.hint: Tokens shake, tremble or sway with some conditions (Cyberpsychosis, Drunk...). Off for a still table; your system's reduced-motion setting switches it off too.

weatherFx.name: Weather you can see
weatherFx.hint: The day's weather shows on Outdoors scenes as Foundry scene weather: rain, storms, acid and blood rain, ash, dust, smog, radioactive wind, snow and heat haze, tinted for Night City. It stays off under weather-restricting roof tiles and in Suppress Weather regions. A weather you set on a scene by hand is left alone.

weatherEveryone.name: Weather reaches everyone on the scene
weatherEveryone.hint: Every character token out in the weather gets its conditions, in combat or not (gear still protects). Off: only the encounter (and player tokens, with "Environment outside combat"). Visibility stays with the encounter either way.

weatherAmbience.name: Weather sounds and lightning
weatherAmbience.hint: Quiet rain, wind and Geiger ambience on Outdoors scenes, and soft lightning flashes with thunder in a thunderstorm (no flashes with token motion off or reduced motion). Plays on the Environment volume slider, scaled by your Neon FX volume.

conditionSheetNotes.name: Condition notes on character sheets
conditionSheetNotes.hint: Each condition on the Effects tab of a character sheet gets a line saying what it does and its page, including conditions Cyberpunk RED can't automate.

arsenalAnimations.name: Automated Animations for 2070 weapons
arsenalAnimations.hint: Each attack gets Neon Arsenal's animation for what the weapon is (its kind, its Power, Smart or Tech flavor, its ammo, its Melee Rebuild), whatever it's called. Needs Automated Animations and JB2A.

arsenalAutoInstall.name: Offer to install the animations
arsenalAutoInstall.hint: When the GM loads the world and Neon Arsenal's animations aren't in Automated Animations (or are from an older version), a window offers to put them in. The Install Weapon Animations macro does it any time.

arsenalSounds.name: Weapon sounds
arsenalSounds.hint: Gunshots, bursts, ricochets, impacts, charge-ups and explosions, played by Neon Combat Manager on each player's client at their own Neon FX volume, quiet by default.

arsenalAreas.name: Area attacks place their template
arsenalAreas.hint: Grenades, rockets and other explosives place a 10×10 m/yds area (or the size on the ammo's card), and Shotgun Shells and flamethrowers a 6 m/yds cone, before the dice. Everyone inside is targeted, and the GM applies the damage and the ammo's effects to all of them at once.

arsenalBlowBack.name: Blown back
arsenalBlowBack.hint: HOUSE RULE (2070 Core Rules, Ch07): whoever takes damage from an explosion is thrown 2 m/yds (4 from a rocket or missile) away from its centre, and stops at a wall (Into the Wall). Offered in the GM's apply window.

arsenalRebuilds.name: Weapon traits
arsenalRebuilds.hint: Power guns add 5 to a Critical Injury's Bonus Damage and can ricochet; Smart guns get +1 to hit (with a Neuroport, Personal Link or Subdermal Grip), and Improved Smart rounds a retry; Tech guns charge. Rebuilds other modules register (Neon At Home's Melee Rebuilds) apply on every attack.

arsenalDvDisplay.name: Diwako's DV display: 2070 tables
arsenalDvDisplay.hint: Diwako's DV display shows the 2070 range tables (Neon Hub's, or whichever CPR is set to), and each gun's own Autofire table as its card names it. Reload to change.

arsenalPlayerFlashes.name: Muzzle flashes for players' shots
arsenalPlayerFlashes.hint: Diwako's muzzle flash (with DF Active Lights) only lights the GM's own shots; this sends players' shots to the GM's client so theirs flash too. The GM must be viewing the scene.

arsenalRebuildConditions.name: Weapon conditions
arsenalRebuildConditions.hint: Power Weapon, Smart Weapon and Tech Weapon go on a character while a gun of that flavor (or with that Rebuild) is equipped, and come off when it isn't. They carry no numbers (the weapon traits add those on the roll); they show on the token and switch on the looks below.

arsenalShotFx.name: Ricochet and smart shot looks
arsenalShotFx.hint: A Power ricochet is drawn bouncing off the nearest wall that gets it round to the target, with sparks at the bounce. A Smart gun's rounds lock on and curve in to the target (Improved Smart rounds glowing magenta), and an Improved Smart retry loops back round. Needs Sequencer; these shots replace Automated Animations' straight shot.

arsenalXray.name: Tech scopes see through thin cover
arsenalXray.hint: While a character with a Tech Weapon is selected, their player sees a glowing outline of anyone behind thin cover (walls marked "Thin cover" in the wall's settings, and closed doors) who they can't otherwise see. Only on that player's screen. Hidden tokens are never shown.

arsenalThinDoors.name: Closed doors are thin cover
arsenalThinDoors.hint: Tech scopes see through closed doors. Off: only walls marked "Thin cover" count.

coverOn.name: Cover
coverOn.hint: Walls tagged with a material and thickness, and Neon Cover pieces, have the 2070 Cover HP per 2×2 m/yds section. Shots and areas say what cover is in the way, and the GM's buttons put the damage on it (2070 Core Rules, Ch07).

coverDoors.name: Doors are Wood (Thin) cover
coverDoors.hint: A door with no cover of its own counts as Wood (Thin): 5 HP. Off: only walls you tag are cover.

coverPieceWalls.name: Cover pieces are barriers
coverPieceWalls.hint: Each cover piece on the map gets walls of its own, kept by the GM's client: nobody walks through it, and a tall piece (a wall section, a fence, a partition) also blocks sight and light. A destroyed piece opens until it's repaired. Off: pieces are plain tokens.

coverLabels.name: Show cover damage on the map (GM)
coverLabels.hint: The GM sees each damaged wall section's HP on the map, and an ✕ where one is destroyed.

arsenalRicochetDodge.name: Tracking a ricochet
arsenalRicochetDodge.hint: A ricochet can't be dodged, unless the target can follow the bounce: a Kerenzikov or other speedware that's on, or low-light, infrared or UV optics while they're in the dark. Then they may Evade at -4 (2070 Core Rules, Ch07, Ricochets in Play). Off: no ricochet is ever dodged.

arsenalSmartPrompt.name: Ask to retry Improved Smart misses
arsenalSmartPrompt.hint: When an Improved Smart round misses by 5 or less, the shooter is asked straight away whether to take the second try (14 + 1d10, the first shot's penalties, and any LUCK they add). The button on the card stays either way.

arsenalHitCheck.name: Does it hit?
arsenalHitCheck.hint: Under each ranged attack card: for each target, the DV at that range (the 2070 tables, Autofire on the gun's own table), hit or miss and by how much, Autofire's damage multiplier, and whether they can dodge (REF 8+).

arsenalHideDiwakoHit.name: Hide Diwako's "Does it hit?" message
arsenalHideDiwakoHit.hint: Diwako's module posts its own hit message, read off "<table> (Autofire)" tables the 2070 guns don't have, and it has no setting of its own. With Does it hit? above on, this keeps that message out of the chat. Diwako's hit sounds and animations are its own settings.

movementRuler.name: Movement ruler
movementRuler.hint: While a token is dragged, its path in Cyberpunk RED's bands: within the Move Action (MOVE × 2 m/yds, cyan), with a Run (yellow), out of reach (red), from MOVE now and counting what was walked this Turn. Space or right-click drops a waypoint, Backspace takes it back. On Foundry v13 it colours Foundry's own ruler; with Drag Ruler running, Drag Ruler gets the bands. Reload to change.

movementRulerWaypoints.name: Tokens walk their waypoints
movementRulerWaypoints.hint: With waypoints dropped while dragging, the token walks them one leg at a time on release (a wall stops a player's token), rather than straight to the end (Foundry v12).

arsenalDefense.name: Defense: Evade or Tank
arsenalDefense.hint: After an attack, each target who can dodge bullets (REF 8+, or chrome that lets them: a Reflex Co-Processor, Corgo's Kerenzikov, a running Militech 'Apogee' or 'Falcon' OS) gets a card: Evade (DEX + Evasion + 1d10 against the attack) or Tank (the range DV stands). Nobody dodges a ricochet, a shooter they don't know is there (the attacker Hidden), or bullets with their eyes shut down. In an area, whoever dodges out is left out of it. Like Vec's Cyberpunk RED Evasion Workflow, built in.

arsenalDefenseMelee.name: Defense: melee
arsenalDefenseMelee.hint: A melee attack is always an opposed Evasion roll: rolled for the target at once, or a card their player rolls from.

arsenalDefenseTies.name: Defense: ties go to the defender
arsenalDefenseTies.hint: The attacker must beat the Evasion roll, as Cyberpunk RED has it; off, a tie is a hit.

arsenalDefenseVisibility.name: Defense: who sees the result
arsenalDefenseVisibility.hint: Everyone, or the GM and the target's players.

SceneWeather.Label: Weather (Neon Combat Manager)
SceneWeather.Hint: Outdoors: Night City's weather shows here and hits characters out in it (not under shelters). Indoors: no weather here. Off: for HUB, title and menu screens: no weather at all, and the scene's own weather is never touched. Default follows the module setting.

Card.DeathSaveBody: Roll 1d10 + penalty under BODY {body} to hold on (penalty {penalty}; a 10 always fails).
Card.DirectDamage: Straight to HP; armor isn't touched.
Card.ArmorDamage: Armor applies: roll it through the character sheet or apply it by hand.
Card.WoreOffBody: Roll WILL + Resist Torture/Drugs against DV{dv}, or gain {addiction}.
Card.CombatOverBody: {elapsed} passed in the world. It's now {clock}.
Card.WokeUp: {name} takes a hit and comes to.

Reminder.spinalInjury: Spinal Injury: no Action this Turn. The Move Action is still there.
Reminder.suppressed: Suppressed: the Move Action (and Run, if needed) goes to getting into cover.
Reminder.noMove: {name} moved more than 4 m/yds last Turn: no Move Action this Turn.
Reminder.qhCrippleMovement: Cripple Movement: cyberlegs locked, no Move Action this Turn or next (one cyberleg: MOVE halved instead).
Reminder.qhPuppet: Puppet: the Netrunner takes this Turn's Action and Move Action, with this character's STATs and Skills.
Reminder.qhCyberpsychosis: Cyberpsychosis (quickhack): attack the nearest person with whatever's in hand. After 3 Rounds, 2d6 Humanity Loss.
Reminder.extremeCyberpsychosis: Extreme Cyberpsychosis: the GM has the sheet. Each Round the player may spend 1 LUCK to try to retake the Move Action (Endurance) or the Action (Concentration), at a DV the GM sets.

Hazard.acidRain: A full minute in acid rain: worn armor of everyone out in it without protection ablates by 1.
Hazard.bloodRainToxic: It's toxic: Resist Torture/Drugs DV15 or take 3d6 straight to HP (an umbrella or waterproof lining gives +2).
Hazard.ashStorm: A minute in the ash: Resist Torture/Drugs DV13 or take 2d6 straight to HP and a Foreign Object (no bonus damage).
Hazard.inversionSmog: A minute in the smog: Resist Torture/Drugs DV13 or take 2d6 straight to HP.
Hazard.dustStorm: Five minutes in the dust: a Foreign Object (no bonus damage) for everyone without a mask or Nasal Filters.
Hazard.lightningStrikes: Lightning strikes close (1d6: {roll})! It hits the tallest structure, or the tallest character or the one holding a two-handed metal weapon: 6d6 and a flashbang.

Carousel.ClockHint: Time since the fight began ({seconds} s a Round) and the time of day
Carousel.SneakHint: Begin a stealth segment: Turns and Rounds in Initiative order, nobody spotted yet

Hint.stealth: Stealth segment: Turns and Rounds in Initiative order, nobody spotted yet. The enemies' Awareness stays where the GM puts it.

Switch.combat: Spotted: switch to full combat (Initiative order kept)

Card.Body: Round {round}. Same Initiative order: carry on from the Turn under way.

Lab.Title: Condition Lab
Lab.Intro: Every condition the tokens can carry and what it does in Cyberpunk RED's rolls. Edit them, switch them off, or add your own. Click an icon to toggle it on the selected tokens.
Lab.CltActive: Condition Lab & Triggler is running too. It replaces the token statuses when it loads; turn it off once you've imported its conditions.
Lab.Shim: Standing in for Condition Lab & Triggler: macros and modules calling game.clt use these conditions.
Lab.SelectTokens: Select one or more tokens first.
Lab.CltImported: Condition Lab & Triggler: {matched} matched, {added} added as custom conditions, {effects} effects moved over.
Lab.ChangesHint: Cyberpunk RED roll keys (bonuses.allActions, bonuses.ranged, system.stats.move.value...). Situational ones show as toggles in the roll dialog.
Lab.ModeHint: Another module's change, worked out by its own code. Its value is kept as it is.
Lab.LimitHint: A floor or ceiling, applied after every other change (MOVE can't drop below 1).

Triggers.Title: Triggler
Triggers.Intro: Rules that add or remove a condition when an actor's data passes a test, like HP at or below 0. Data paths are Cyberpunk RED's (system.derivedStats.hp.value, system.stats.luck.value...). Undo removes it again when the test stops passing.

Environment.Title: Environment
Environment.NoCalendar: Neon Hub has no calendar this user can see.
Environment.NoHub: Neon Hub isn't running: pick the weather by hand.
Environment.SightHint: Sight penalty from light and weather
Environment.NoOne: No one in an encounter on this scene.

Biomon.Title: Biomon Link
Biomon.RemoveConfirm: Break the {name} link? Everyone on it stops sharing vitals.
Biomon.Full: Open the full Biomonitor (Neon At Home)
Biomon.JoinHint: Share your character's vitals with a group. Everyone on the link sees each other's HP, condition and injuries.
Biomon.ImplantNeeded: Linking needs a Biomonitor or Neuroport installed.
Biomon.NeedsImplant: {name} has no Biomonitor or Neuroport installed to link.
Biomon.NoSignalHint: No Biomonitor or Neuroport installed: nothing to read.
Biomon.SpoofedHint: Vitals Spoof: this readout is fake. Only you (the GM) see this tag.

Holocall.Title: Holocall
Holocall.NoMessenger: Holocalls go through Night City Messenger: turn it on (2.1 or later, with Calls switched on).
Holocall.Jammed: {name}'s comms are jammed: no calls out.
Holocall.NoNumber: {name} has no number in Night City Messenger. The GM gives numbers in its Phone settings.
Holocall.Failed: The call to {name} didn't go through.

NoSignalFx.Title: No signal
NoSignalFx.Sub: Carrier lost. Messages and calls won't get through here.
NoSignalFx.SubAt: Carrier lost in {place}. Messages and calls won't get through here.

Stakes.Title: Plot Die
Stakes.LuckHint: LUCK pool / LUCK STAT. LUCK 5+ can ask for the Stakes; 7+ can Double Down and Force Fate.

Perk.ask: LUCK {luck}+: ask the GM to Raise the Stakes
Perk.doubleDown: LUCK {luck}+: Double Down, reroll the Plot Die (once a session)
Perk.forceFate: LUCK {luck}+: Force Fate, {cost} LUCK for an Opportunity (once a session)

Stakes.DoubleDownWhen: once the Plot Die is rolled
Stakes.ForceFateWhen: once the GM Raises the Stakes
Stakes.ReasonGM: What's riding on it (optional, shown on the card)
Stakes.ReasonPlayer: Make your case: why does this Check matter?
Stakes.GrantHint: At your call, an exploding 10 brings an Opportunity and an imploding 1 a Complication, without the Plot Die.
Stakes.NewSessionHint: Double Down and Force Fate are once a session: start a new session to give them back to everyone.
Stakes.NewSessionDone: New session: Double Down and Force Fate are back for everyone.
Stakes.Asked: Asked the GM to Raise the Stakes.
Stakes.NoOne: No character to roll for. Select a token or pick a character.

Face.complication: +{bonus}, and the GM picks a Complication

OppText.criticallyHit: Attacks that hit: a fitting Critical Injury of your choice, without its Bonus Damage.
OppText.narrative: Describe something good that happens, success or fail.

CompText.hinderAlly: A PC's next Action takes a penalty that fits the scene.
CompText.feelingUnlucky: Lose 1 LUCK. Out of LUCK: fall Prone, a weapon jams, or gear malfunctions.
CompText.narrative: The GM describes something bad that happens, success or fail.

Stakes.Raised: The Stakes are Raised on {name}'s Check
Stakes.RaisedBody: Roll the Plot Die before the d10. A Complication adds its bonus to this Check.
Stakes.NeedLuck: Asking for the Stakes takes a LUCK STAT of {luck}+.
Stakes.Asks: {name} asks the GM to Raise the Stakes
Stakes.Denied: Not this time, {name}: the Stakes stay where they are.

ResultBody.complication: +{bonus} is on this Check (ticked in the roll dialog). The GM picks {count} Complication(s).
ResultBody.complicationInline: +{bonus} is on the roll being made now. The GM picks {count} Complication(s).

Stakes.DoubleDownCost: Doubled Down into a Complication: -{luck} LUCK, {count} Complication(s).
Stakes.CantForce: Force Fate takes LUCK 7+, 3 LUCK to spend, and once a session.
Stakes.CantDouble: Double Down takes LUCK 7+, LUCK left, and once a session.
Stakes.Head: Head
Stakes.CritHint: Pick a Critical Injury that fits the attack. No Bonus Damage; a rolled crit still applies too.
Stakes.OutOfLuck: {name} is out of LUCK. Pick what goes wrong:

Unlucky.jam: {name}'s weapon jams: an Action to clear it.
Unlucky.malfunction: A piece of {name}'s gear or chrome malfunctions.

Done.aidAlly: {name} sets up {ally}: +2 on their next Check.
Done.hinderAlly: {ally} is hindered: -{penalty} on their next Check.

Awareness.Title: Combat Awareness
Awareness.LeftHint: Points left to assign / your Solo Rank.
Awareness.NoSolo: No Solo here. Combat Awareness needs a character with the Solo role.
Awareness.NotYourTurn: {name} reassigns Combat Awareness as their Action: wait for their Turn.

ModeHint.free: Free now: outside combat or before Initiative.
ModeHint.action: In combat this takes your Action for the Turn.
ModeHint.wait: In combat it's an Action on your own Turn. Wait for it.
ModeHint.gm: Not their Turn: you can still adjust it as GM (no Action spent).

Done.action: {name} spends their Action on Combat Awareness.

Effect.damageDeflection: -{n} to the first damage each Round
Effect.notYet: Not enough for a step yet

Hint.precisionAttack: Every 3 points: +1 to all attacks (up to +3).
Hint.spotWeakness: 1 point each: +1 damage before armor on your first successful attack each Round.
Hint.damageDeflection: Every 2 points: the first damage you take each Round is 1 less (up to 5).
Hint.fumbleRecovery: 4 points: ignore implodes (1s) on attack rolls. The 1 still counts as 1.

Hub.Title: Night City Map
Hub.KeyHint: Open the City & NCART hub (Night City 2070).
Hub.GMOnly: The GM has the city map to themselves for now.
Hub.HomeHint: Drag to move, scroll to zoom. Click a place, a district or a station. Pick two to plan a route.
Hub.NotePlaceholder: Only you see this. Who's here tonight, what's going on…
Hub.StormHint: Fog, a storm or a closed bridge: every trip on the ground takes twice as long.
Hub.TravelHint: Moves the clock by the trip and the crew marker to the destination. Cars roll for a jam.
Hub.NoWay: There's no way to make this trip like that.
Hub.HiddenNote: Hidden from the players. They don't see it on the map, in searches or in lists.
Hub.RevealQuietHint: Show it on the players' map without a chat card.
Hub.MoveHint: Click the map where {name} goes. Esc cancels.
Hub.ResetHint: Undo your changes to this place.
Hub.DeleteConfirm: Delete {name} from the map? Its notes go with it.
Hub.CantDelete: The map's own places can be hidden, not deleted.
Hub.NothingKnown: Nothing you know of here. Yet.
Hub.DiscoveryOnHint: Places stay hidden until you reveal them.
Hub.NeedSpot: Click the map where the place is first.
Hub.DiscoveredHint: It's on the Night City Map now (Shift+M).

Door.Title: Doorway
Door.Hint: The scene this place leads into, so players can walk in from the map (between sessions too): a shop, a bar, someone to talk to.
Door.TagHint: lands on the first tile with this tag
Door.NoMatt: With Monk's Active Tiles, landing on one of its tiles runs that tile's actions.
Door.Open: Players can walk in from the map
Door.NoCharacter: You need a character to go there.
Door.LookOnly: You can look around. Your token comes along when a GM is online (or with permission to place tokens).
Door.NoActions: Its tile's actions run when a GM is online.

Blocked.noScene: This place doesn't lead anywhere yet.
Blocked.closed: The GM hasn't opened this place to visits.
Blocked.noGM: Visits need a GM online right now.

Roller.NotRaised: The GM hasn't raised the Stakes on this roll.
Roller.NoStakes: LUCK 5+ can ask for the Stakes.
Roller.PushHint: Spend 2 LUCK before you roll to add your LUCK STAT ({stat}). One way to Ride the Edge per roll. Second Chance and Close Call are on the roll card afterwards.
Roller.SecondChanceHint: Reroll this Check (it failed). Not on a natural 1.
Roller.CloseCallHint: The natural 1 doesn't implode. The die still reads 1.
Roller.CloseCallBody: The implosion die ({crit}) doesn't count. It was {was}.
Roller.CantEdge: That's not on for this roll (LUCK, a natural 1, or LUCK already ridden).
Roller.ChainHint: Chain dice don't change the total. The payout is automatic; the Opportunities or Complications bring no +2/+4.

Pay.autoCrit: A Critical Injury of your choice that fits the attack (with its Bonus Damage).
Pay.malfunction: The weapon malfunctions (an Action to clear).
Pay.malfunctionOrCondition: Plus a gear or chrome malfunction, or a fitting condition.
Pay.condition: Plus a condition the GM picks that fits (Prone, Blinded, Suppressed, a dropped weapon).

Tarot.Offer: Three or more 6s: {sixes} on the damage dice
Tarot.OfferBody: Draw a Tarot card instead of the normal Critical Injury: one target, not an area attack (grenades, rockets, Shotgun Shells), not a drone or turret. One card a session.
Tarot.DrawHint: Draws for your current target. One card a session; the deck isn't shuffled until every card has been seen.
Tarot.AlreadyDrawn: This session's card has been drawn. Draw another anyway?
Tarot.Rules: Each Critical Injury it brings deals its Bonus Damage unless the card says otherwise. Resolve it, then the card goes to the bottom of the deck.
Tarot.NoTarget: Target the victim (or select their token) first.

Card.fool: All the victim's cyberware shuts down for 1 hour, Neuroport included; cyberlimbs work like dismembered limbs. If that leaves them no way to sense the enemy, another -4 to every Check. No chrome: Foreign Object and 3d6 Humanity Loss instead.
Card.magician: The GM picks one piece of the victim's cyberware: Destroyed (repairable). The victim is Deadly On Fire. No chrome: Deadly On Fire, and a weapon they carry malfunctions.
Card.priestess: Poisoned shrapnel: Foreign Object, but each Turn they move 4m+ on foot they must beat DV15 Resist Torture/Drugs or take 3d6 straight to HP (instead of the Bonus Damage again).
Card.empress: The next three successful attacks against the victim this combat each cause a Critical Injury, whatever the dice say (not biotoxins, poisons or stun batons).
Card.emperor: The GM picks a player, who chooses one injury from the Head table and one from the Body table. The victim suffers both.
Card.hierophant: Double damage, after armor and multipliers. The weapon is Destroyed Beyond Repair. An Iconic weapon's owner may keep it instead and deal normal damage.
Card.lovers: The attack hits the head, wherever it was aimed. A melee attack also leaves the victim Grappled by the attacker.
Card.chariot: A flaw in the armor: the armor at the hit location ablates 5 more SP, even if the attack didn't get through.
Card.strength: +25 damage, added before armor and multipliers.
Card.justice: The wind knocked out of them: for 1 minute, -5 Evasion against melee and no dodging ranged attacks.
Card.hermit: Lost Eye twice: both eyes gone (the penalty counts once). With no other way to sense the enemy, another -4 to every Check.
Card.wheel: The attack goes wild. Ranged: the GM picks a random new target. Melee: the attacker falls Prone and misses. Either way the weapon malfunctions.
Card.hanged: Prone, plus Spinal Injury and Whiplash.
Card.death: The victim rolls one Death Save now. Failed: 0 HP, Unconscious for 1 minute, and they wake having regained 3d6 Humanity (up to their maximum).
Card.temperance: The victim chooses one limb to be Dismembered and a different limb to be Broken.
Card.devil: The attack hits the head, wherever it was aimed, and adds Brain Injury and Lost Ear.
Card.tower: Cracked Skull, Crushed Windpipe and Whiplash, with no Bonus Damage. For 1 hour they feel no pain and ignore the Seriously Wounded penalty.
Card.star: Ranged: the round ricochets into a second enemy within 20m (GM's pick), or the same target again: it always hits, in the body; roll new damage. Melee: Broken Ribs and Collapsed Lung.
Card.moon: Foreign Object twice, in the body and in the head. A melee weapon that drew it is stuck in the victim, and the attacker is disarmed.
Card.sun: The GM picks a grenade or other explosive on the victim: it goes off. None: a non-weapon item they carry is Destroyed Beyond Repair.
Card.judgement: Crushed Fingers on one hand and Dismembered Hand on the other.
Card.world: The attacker takes an extra Turn right after this one: +5 to every Skill Check, no Wound State penalties, and no Death Save if Mortally Wounded.

Ladder.Title: Awareness
Ladder.DV: Stealth DV {dv} ({n} enemies). Each failed Stealth roll: one step up.

Hint.searching: Stealth DV: the closest enemy's Perception roll.
Hint.alert: Stealth DV: the highest Perception roll among them.

Ladder.Up: A failed Stealth roll: one step up
Ladder.Obvious: Something obvious (a gunshot, a scream, a body): straight to Alert

Alert.Label: Alert
Alert.Hint: Until the security response is called. Put every one of them down first and the alarm never goes out.
Alert.CalledHint: The security response is on its way. The Alert stays until the GM moves the Awareness Ladder.
Alert.Dismiss: Wave the countdown away (the Alert stays)

Card.ClearedBody: No one is left to raise it: the enemies' Alert ends before a security response was called.
Card.CalledBody: The countdown ran out. Roll the district's Security Code for the response (Core Rules, Chapter 01); the crew's Heat goes up (Chapter 14). The enemies stay at Alert.

Flash.Title: {name}: a Flash of Luck ({type})

TypeHint.simple: Could easily have happened earlier, on camera. 2 LUCK, up to 100eb.
TypeHint.unlikely: Couldn't have happened on camera, but believable. 4 LUCK, up to 500eb.
TypeHint.improbable: Needs remarkable foreknowledge or incredible luck. 8 LUCK, up to 1,000eb.

Flash.Cost: {luck} LUCK, up to {spend}eb (from your pocket). Any Check it needs is rolled now. In combat it takes your Action.
Flash.Placeholder: "Before we went in, I…" What you did, when, and how it helps now.
Flash.Sent: Your Flash of Luck went to the GM.

Blocked.beat: One Flash of Luck a Beat.
Blocked.mission: Three Flashes of Luck a Mission.

Flash.NewBeatHint: A new scene or stretch of the job: one Flash of Luck each again.
Flash.NewMissionHint: A new job: three Flashes of Luck each again.
Flash.NewBeatDone: A new beat: one Flash of Luck each.
Flash.NewMissionDone: A new mission: three Flashes of Luck each.

Hud.Title: Action HUD
Hud.KeyHint: Show or hide the Action HUD.
Hud.NoCombat: There's no encounter to roll Initiative in.
Hud.NotInCombat: {name} isn't in the encounter: select their token and roll again.
Hud.NoNetRole: Pick the Netrunner role that runs the deck on the character sheet first.
Hud.ClearOwnHint: Drop this character's own layout: they get the one for all your characters.
Hud.EditorHint: Each player has their own HUD. Rename, reorder and hide groups; Auto shows everything a group has (every equipped weapon, every role ability), or pick the actions and their order yourself. Your own groups can mix actions from anywhere. Ctrl-click an action in the HUD to skip its roll dialog.
Hud.AutoHint: Show everything this group has for the character. Untick to choose.
Hud.Missing: This character doesn't have it: it's skipped.
Hud.ResetHint: Start over from the template (combat basics). Nothing is kept until you save.
Hud.MacroAdded: {name} is in the HUD's Macros now.
Hud.MacroNoRun: You can't run {name} yet: the GM gives you Limited ownership of it (and Use Script Macros).

Error.NoTarget: Target the one token whose Neuroport you're jacking in to.
Error.Self: A Netrunner is always in their own Neuroport.
Error.LockedOut: {target} kicked you out: no hacking them for another {minutes} min.
Error.NoLink: Not jacked in to anyone here. Jack In first.
Error.PickLink: Jacked in to more than one Neuroport: target the token to act on.
Error.NoWalls: {target} has no Passwall left to Breach.
Error.NotSlotted: That quickhack isn't slotted in the deck you're running.
Error.Burned: {hack} burned out: it was single use.
Error.Cooldown: {hack} is on Cooldown for {n} more Rounds.
Error.CooldownTime: {hack} is on Cooldown for about {n} more min.
Error.WallsUp: {target} still has {n} Passwalls up: Breach first.
Error.ThisTurn: One quickhack per target per Turn: {target} has had theirs.
Error.NoIntruder: No Netrunner you know of is in that Neuroport.

Card.JackedInKnown: {name} jacks in to {target}, and they know it
Card.LadderStep: A failed Ghost Jack In: their group climbs one step on the Awareness Ladder.
Card.Rattle: The port rattles: {target} against Interface + Cloak {runner}.
Card.GhostBroken: The Ghost is broken: they know.
Card.QuietGlitch: Quiet, and Ghosted: to them it's chrome acting up.
Card.Defender: Self-ICE: Defender took {n} off (its uses this hour aren't counted here).
Card.ByHand: Its effect is the GM's to apply.
Card.Needs: Needs: {needs}. Without it the quickhack fails, with no Cooldown.
Card.Lockout: An unsafe Jack Out: no hacking them for 60 minutes.

Hands.Title: Equip / Change Weapon
Hands.FreeHint: Put it away: back to Carried, and the hand is free.
Hands.NothingCarried: No weapons marked Carried: set one to Carried on the sheet's Gear tab (or pick one up).
Hands.NoneFree: {name} has no free hand for {item}: free one first.
Hands.NeedMore: {item} needs {need} hands and {name} has {free} free: free one first.
Hands.Owned: {name} puts down {item}: it stays on the sheet as Owned, no longer on them.

Chat.EditLastHint: Edit the last message you sent (Up in an empty chat box does the same).

Core.GmRoll: Roll for you and the GM

Log.AddQuote: Add to the Adventure Log as a quote

Archive.Title: Chat Archive · {name}
Archive.Clear: The {count} archived messages are in the journal. Delete them from the chat log now?

Cmd.Log: Keep a line in the Adventure Log
Cmd.LogHelp: /log something happened · /log q Source what they said · /log q "Two Words" what they said
Cmd.GmLog: Keep a line in the GM's own log
Cmd.Archive: Keep the chat log in a journal, then clear it
Cmd.Cond: Toggle a condition on your selected tokens
Cmd.Stage: Put a character on stage (yours, or the selected tokens)
Cmd.Unstage: Take a character off stage (all: everyone)
Cmd.As: Speak as: me, or a character of yours in this scene or on stage (nothing: the selected token)
Cmd.Narrate: Narrate across the stage (nothing: narrator mode on or off)

Stage.Title: Stage
Stage.NoOne: Select a token or set your character first.
Stage.NotSpeaking: You aren't speaking as anyone on stage.
Stage.SpeakAs: Speak as {name} (click again to stop; right-click: other side; ×: off stage)
Stage.AddHint: Put the selected tokens (or your character) on stage
Stage.NarratorHint: Narrator mode: what you type is narration
Stage.NarratorOn: Narrator mode on: what you type is narration.
Stage.MoodsHint: An image for each expression (empty: the portrait). Characters animate either way.
Stage.DirectorHint: Drop actors or tokens here to bring them on. Right side, left side, a flip and an expression for each; the speech bubble makes you speak as them.
Stage.FocusHint: Stage mode: the table dims and other interface steps back while someone is on stage
Stage.Disabled: The stage is turned off in Neon Chat's settings.

FX.NoSequencer: Neon FX needs the Sequencer module.
FX.SelectToken: Select a token you own first.
FX.Installed: Neon FX: {count} macro(s) added to the "{folder}" folder.

Landing.ClearAsk: Take away the {count} AV landing zone(s) on this scene?

FX.NoChrome: {name} has nothing running to switch off.

Shelter.Label: Shelters from weather (Neon Combat Manager)
Shelter.Hint: Characters under this tile are out of Night City's weather: no weather conditions. Tiles with Foundry's "Restrict Weather" already count, and hide the weather visuals too.

Effect.Manual: Not automated: play it out at the table.
Effect.CriticalItem: Cyberpunk RED's Critical Injury item carries its penalties and Death Save increase
Effect.WoundMirror: Cyberpunk RED applies the Wound State's roll penalties itself
Effect.RebuildMirror: comes and goes with the weapon in hand; Neon Arsenal adds its numbers on the roll
Effect.ToggleOff: {change} (a roll dialog toggle, off until ticked)
Effect.Environment: its numbers are worked out per character from the weather, light, gear and shelter
Effect.Reminder: a reminder at the start of their Turn
Effect.Also: brings {names} with it, and takes them off when it goes
Effect.Stabilize: a Mortally Wounded character goes to 1 HP
Effect.Secondary: asks for the DV{dv} Check when it wears off
Effect.Consume: gone once their next Check is rolled

Arsenal.NoCapacity: {name} takes no capacity attachments: {upgrade} doesn't belong on it.

ReloadRule.oneHand: With one hand free, it reloads for your Move Action.
ReloadRule.twoHanded: Held in two hands, it reloads for your Move Action.
ReloadRule.always: It can reload for your Move Action.

Arsenal.NoSingle: {name} can only Autofire or lay down Suppressive Fire right now.
Arsenal.ScopeNone: The scope shows nobody behind thin cover.
Arsenal.RicochetOn: {weapon}: the next shot ricochets (−4, can't be dodged).
Arsenal.ChargeBodyFree: This weapon charges without giving up the Move Action. It holds for 20 Rounds or until fired: the next non-explosive attack is ROF1, goes through Thin cover without damaging it, and ignores half the target's SP (2070 Core Rules, Ch07).
Arsenal.ChargeBodyHalf: This weapon charges for half your MOVE (round down), given up before you move. It holds for 20 Rounds or until fired: the next non-explosive attack is ROF1, goes through Thin cover without damaging it, and ignores half the target's SP (2070 Core Rules, Ch07).
Arsenal.ChargeBody: That's the Move Action. It holds for 20 Rounds or until fired: the next non-explosive attack is ROF1, goes through Thin cover without damaging it, and ignores half the target's SP (2070 Core Rules, Ch07).

Note.ricochet: Ricochet (−4): bounced off cover at a target the shooter knows is there. It can't be dodged, unless the target can follow the bounce (speedware that's on, or low-light, IR or UV optics in the dark): then at −4 (2070 Core Rules, Ch07, Ricochets in Play).
Note.burstShort: A short burst: the last {rounds} in the magazine.
Note.burstShortDamage: A short burst: the last {rounds} in the magazine, for {damage}.
Note.specialMod: This weapon's own rule: {value} to the attack.
Note.shortBurstDamage: Fired short of a full burst: {damage}.
Note.dropLowest: This weapon rolls {formula} and drops the lowest.
Note.ap: This weapon's rounds count as Armor-Piercing: 2 SP ablated.
Note.critBonus: This weapon's Critical Injuries deal +{bonus} Bonus Damage (counted if the dice make one).
Note.ruleCrit: A Critical Injury by this weapon's rule ({face}s count as 6s): roll the injury and add its {bonus} Bonus Damage, which the total above doesn't include.
Note.critRemind: On this Critical Injury, this weapon's own rule: {text}
Note.memo: From last Round, this weapon's own rule: {text}
Note.autoStreak: Autofire {count} in a row: once more and this weapon is Destroyed Beyond Repair.
Note.autoStreakOver: Autofire {count} in a row: this weapon is Destroyed Beyond Repair.
Note.bodyShort: This weapon asks for BODY {need}; the shooter has {have}. Unless it's mounted, that's the GM's call.
Note.recoil: Fired without the BODY or the cyberarm for it: {injury} on the shooter.
Note.effectDv: Whoever it hits must beat DV{dv} {skill} or be {effect}.
Note.throughCover: Its rounds carry their damage through cover, as an explosive's does.
Note.smartNoLink: Smart weapon without a Personal Link or Subdermal Grip: no +1.
Note.unobscured: Improved Smart: ignores {value} from obscurement (darkness, smoke, fog).
Note.powerCrit: Power: the Critical Injury's Bonus Damage is +5 more.
Note.chargedAttack: Charged Tech shot: ROF1, through Thin cover without damaging it.
Note.chargedDamage: Charged Tech shot: ignores half the target's SP (on the Apply Damage button).
Note.push: Propulsion Impact: whoever this hits is pushed {metres} m/yds away (done).

Arsenal.SmartRetryFlavor: Improved Smart Ammunition: 14 + 1d10, with the first shot's penalties

RetryAsk.Title: Improved Smart Ammunition
RetryAsk.Body: Missed DV{dv} by {by}. The round can re-acquire: a second try at {formula}.

ThinCover.Label: Thin cover (Neon Arsenal)
ThinCover.Hint: A thin wall, a car door, a shoji screen: Tech scopes show who's behind it as an outline, and a charged Tech shot goes through it. Closed doors count already (a world setting).

Arsenal.PlaceHint: Place the {size} m/yds area: left-click to place it, right-click or Escape for a normal attack.
Arsenal.NoDv: {total}: no range table for this distance; the GM decides.
Arsenal.MissMoves: On a miss the GM moves the blast: drag the template where it lands (within the area around the aimed square), or Scatter it at random, and it goes off there.
Arsenal.AreaRules: One damage roll for everyone in it, body armor only, and it ablates. Cover in the area takes it first; anyone who can dodge bullets and beats the roll gets out (2070 Core Rules, Ch07, Firing Modes).
Arsenal.ShellAutofire: Shotgun Automatic Control Group: the shell attack is rolled with the Autofire Skill for 4 shells, and dodging it takes {penalty}. Its damage is the shells', not multiplied.
Arsenal.UntickHint: Untick anyone who dodged out, or whose cover took the hit.
Arsenal.KeepArea: Keep the template on the scene
Arsenal.RollDamageFirst: Roll the damage first: the area takes the damage roll's numbers.
Arsenal.SaveBody: Caught by {ammo}. Beat the DV to shrug it off.
Arsenal.Installed: Neon Arsenal: {count} animations put into Automated Animations ({pack}).
Arsenal.NoActor: Select a token of yours (or have a character).
Arsenal.NoSwitches: {name} has no weapon with a switch (a Power gun's ricochet, a Tech gun's charge).

HitCheck.dodge: They can dodge bullets: if they Evade, their Evasion roll replaces the DV.

Arsenal.Scattered: The blast scatters {metres} m/yds from the aimed square

Defense.Title: {name}: {attacker} fires the {weapon}
Defense.Body: Evade: roll DEX + Evasion + 1d10 against the attack roll (you can dodge bullets). Tank: the range DV stands.
Defense.MeleeBody: Melee is always an opposed roll: DEX + Evasion + 1d10 against the attack roll.
Defense.RicochetDodge: It's a ricochet you can follow: Evade takes {penalty}.
Defense.WeaponDodge: This weapon's Aimed Shots are hard to dodge: Evade takes {penalty}.
Defense.ShellDodge: It's a Shotgun Automatic Control Group's shell attack: Evade takes {penalty}.

evade.hit: {name} doesn't get out of the way: Evasion {evasion} vs {attack}, a hit. Roll damage.
evade.out: {name} dives out of the area (Evasion {evasion} vs {attack}).

tank.hit: {name} takes it: {attack} beats DV{dv}, a hit. Roll damage.
tank.missed: {name} stands there, and it misses anyway ({attack} vs DV{dv}).
tank.tank: {name} takes it: against the range DV (the GM's call at this range).

Offer.Title: Neon Arsenal: weapon animations
Offer.Missing: Neon Arsenal's weapon animations (JB2A, chosen by what each weapon is) aren't in Automated Animations yet. Put them in now? Your own Automated Animations entries stay as they are.
Offer.Outdated: Neon Arsenal's weapon animations in Automated Animations are from an older version. Bring them up to date? Your own Automated Animations entries stay as they are.
Offer.Damaged: Some of Neon Arsenal's weapon animations have dropped out of Automated Animations (an older install gave them ids AA's menu throws away). Put them all back now? Your own Automated Animations entries stay as they are.
Offer.Later: Any time later: the Install Weapon Animations macro (Neon Combat Manager: Macros compendium).

Reload.Title: Neon Arsenal: reload to finish
Reload.Body: The weapon animations are repaired. Automated Animations stopped loading partway on every browser that opened the world with the old entries, so the shots won't show until each one reloads. Reload everyone now? Players are asked first.
Reload.PlayerBody: The GM has repaired the weapon animations. Reload to see them? Automated Animations won't show shots in this browser until it reloads.

BlindBox.Title: {weapon}: the Blind Box
BlindBox.Combo: A Combo Casing: one round with both effects.
BlindBox.CritSuccess: A Critical Success: it's GACHA! whatever was in the box.
BlindBox.Jam: A Critical Failure: a dud, and the gun jams.

junk.name: Junk Ammo
junk.effect: a dud. No damage, and the gun rolls a Malfunction.

flashbang.name: Flashbang
flashbang.effect: bursts where it hits, as Flashbang ammo.

smoke.name: Smoke
smoke.effect: bursts where it hits, as Smoke ammo.

teargas.name: Teargas
teargas.effect: bursts where it hits, as Teargas ammo.

arrowhypo.name: Arrowhypo
arrowhypo.effect: delivers a dose of a Street Drug, the GM's pick.

airburst.name: Airburst
airburst.effect: bursts where it hits, as Airburst ammo.

improvedSmart.name: Improved Smart
improvedSmart.effect: Smart weapons only, so here it fires as Basic.

co2.name: CO2
co2.effect: no damage; puts out every fire where it bursts.

hvap.name: HVAP
hvap.effect: Armor-Piercing, High Precision and High Velocity at once.

overpressure.name: Overpressure
overpressure.effect: the shot fires, and the gun is Destroyed (not beyond repair).

gacha.name: GACHA! Ammunition
gacha.effect: +1d6 damage on a hit, and a 2nd Amendment prize ticket.

Malfunction.1: dirty barrel: it deals 1d6 less damage, for 1 minute.
Malfunction.2: accident: the next Attack targets an ally within 6 m/yds of the target.
Malfunction.3: off target: −2 to the next Attack Check with it.
Malfunction.4: gunked up: it can't cause a Critical Injury through its damage roll, for 1 minute.
Malfunction.5: jam: it jams after the next Attack Check, whatever its Quality.
Malfunction.6: neglected parts: the ammunition loaded in it is Destroyed Beyond Repair.

Chaos.Title: {weapon}: reloaded
Chaos.Body: New for this magazine: {capacity} rounds, {damage} damage, {ablation} SP ablated. Reloaded too often (the GM's call), it's Damaged.
